domain.name: clark_scarf
domain.one_line: Serial multi-echelon inventory control with backlogging and echelon-based holding costs (Clark & Scarf 1960).

n_echelons.source: the paper's scheme [N] -> ... -> [2] -> [1], stated for general N

leadtime_k.source: p.1783: delivery lag λ; the paper admits per-installation lags and states no upper bound. leadtime_k = 0 is out of scope, see out_of_scope

c_ship.source: p.1784: 'The unit shipping cost from 2 to 1 will be denoted by c_1'; Assumption 2: linear at every link, 'without any setup cost. The only exception ... at the highest installation'. Setting c_k = 0 is a DESIGN choice (operator convenience), not model structure

ship_k.source: real-valued and unbounded above in the model; every bound on it is design or implementation

demand.domain: distribution on [0, inf), independent across periods; stationarity not required by the model
demand.source: p.1783: density φ(t), 'the demands being independent from period to period. (The demand distributions may actually differ from period to period.)' -- neither a family, nor integrality, nor stationarity is model structure

out_of_scope: fixed (setup) ordering costs: Assumption 2 / section 5 permit a setup cost at the HIGHEST installation only; not modeled here at any level
leadtime_k = 0: void under the A -> S -> D event order -- a lag-0 dispatch would land before its own dispatch
dynamics: A: forall k: stock_k += pipe_{k,1};  forall k: pipe_{k,·} <- shift(pipe_{k,·}) (drop the head, append 0)
S: a_k = min(ship_k, stock_{k+1}) for k < n_echelons;  a_N = ship_N (outside supplier, unclipped);  forall k < n_echelons: stock_{k+1} -= a_k;  forall k: pipe_{k,leadtime_k} += a_k

objective: minimize E[ sum_{t=0..horizon_T-1} discount_factor^t * (holding_t + shortage_t + shipping_t) ] where holding_t = h_install_1 * max(stock_1, 0) + sum_{k=2..n_echelons} h_install_k * stock_k + sum_{k=1..n_echelons-1} h_install_{k+1} * sum_{s=1..leadtime_k} pipe_{k,s} (in-transit stock charged at its SOURCE's rate, Assumption 3 / F1), shortage_t = p_short * max(-stock_1, 0), and shipping_t = sum_{k=1..n_echelons} c_ship_k * a_k (on executed shipments)

notation.stock_k: the paper's x_1 at the retailer (installation on-hand); its x_i for i >= 2 is ECHELON stock (p.1784), derived here by echelon_stock()
notation.pipe_{k,s}: the paper's w_j, 'units to be delivered j periods in the future' (p.1783); its state C_n(x_1, w_1, ..., w_{lambda-1}) carries lambda-1 slots -- exactly the gym's observable slots
notation.leadtime_k: the paper's lambda (p.1783). Do NOT shorten to L: the paper's L(x) is the one-period holding+shortage cost function (Eq. 1)
notation.discount_factor: the paper's alpha (costs n periods out discounted by alpha^n, p.1783); the solver spec calls it beta
notation.h_install, p_short: the paper's h and p, 'the marginal holding and shortage costs' (Eq. 1)
notation.c_ship: the paper's c_1 unit shipping cost (p.1784); c(z) = K + c*z with K = 0 everywhere but the top (Eq. 5, Assumption 2)
notation.D_t: the paper's demand draw, written there as t with density phi(t) (p.1783) -- t is our period index, hence the rename
notation.t vs n: our t counts periods ELAPSED; the paper's n counts periods REMAINING, n = horizon_T - t. The DP table ybar[t] is the paper's xbar_n under that index change
notation.u, y, xbar_n: as the paper: f_n(u) over echelon position u, decision Min_{y>=u} (Eq. 4), critical value xbar_n (p.1784) -- DP and readback already use these

constants.name: n_echelons
constants.desc: number of live installations in the serial chain. Level 1 is the retailer facing demand; level n_echelons buys from the outside supplier. Independent of `leadtime`.

constants.name: leadtime
constants.desc: transit time in periods on EVERY link: a shipment dispatched in period t lands at the arrival event of period t+leadtime. MODEL DOMAIN: per-link lead times L_k, each any integer >= 1 (the paper admits per-installation lags; L = 0 is void under this formalization's event order -- dispatch follows the arrival event within a period). THIS CONSTANT RENDERS A NARROWING: identical lags on every link, cited in mdp.model.notation; every current scenario uses identical lags, and lifting it is a scenario-field + DP extension, not a value change. Independent of chain length -- a pipeline is COMMITTED flow, whereas an extra installation is a discretionary buffer whose units may be held and re-decided each period. EXPERIMENT DESIGN, a separate later choice: the campaign sweeps {1, 2}; 2 is the paper's worked value (section 2). NO IMPLEMENTATION CAP: this constant is itself the width of every pipe_k vector (length: 'leadtime'), so each instance renders exactly the slots it selects and any lead time is representable. The earlier rendering unrolled a fixed LEADTIME_CAP = 4 and could not express L > 4; it was removed at F7.

constants.name: horizon_T
constants.desc: episode length in periods. Set at 50 rather than 30 so that, with beta = 0.95 (effective horizon ~20 periods), a genuinely stationary middle stretch exists between the chain filling and the end-of-horizon wind-down -- that is the stretch the Stage-5 base-stock readback recovers x-bar from.

constants.name: demand_mean
constants.desc: Poisson rate of retailer demand. Set at 10 rather than 5 so integrality is fine-grained relative to the decision scale (sd = 3.2); at 5 a single unit is a large relative move and would contaminate the base-stock readback.

constants.name: p_short
constants.desc: shortage penalty per unit of retailer backlog per period; with h_retail = 1 the critical ratio is p/(p+h)

constants.name: h_install
constants.desc: CUMULATIVE echelon holding rate per installation: h_install[k] = sum of echelon rates h_j for j >= k+1. Derived from echelon rates h_retail = 1.0 at level 1 and h_echelon = 0.5 at every level above; a unit at the retailer costs h_retail + h_echelon*(n_echelons-1) per period, one at the top costs h_echelon. Zero at every inert level, so padding is never charged. Default shown is n_echelons = 3: echelon rates (1.0, 0.5, 0.5) -> cumulative (2.0, 1.0, 0.5, 0.0).

constants.name: c_ship
constants.desc: c_ship[k] = per-unit cost of shipping into installation k+1 (the top link renders the ordering/purchase cost from the outside supplier). MODEL DOMAIN: real >= 0 per link -- the paper's model carries linear shipping/ordering costs at every level and the decomposition survives them. DESIGN: every current scenario sets 0, an operator convenience choice at the interview, NOT model structure; nonzero values are expressible per instance without any structural change. Charged on SHIPPED units (post-clip) at the S event.

constants.name: ship_max
constants.desc: upper bound on any single shipment = 20 x demand_mean. Caps the ACTION SCALE, not a physical limit; a bare constant so instances that move demand_mean resize it too.

constants.name: demand_scale
constants.desc: gamma scale theta. Parameterized so shape = demand_mean/theta and scale = theta, hence mean = demand_mean by construction -- every instance that overrides demand_mean (verify_l3 at 4, verify_tiny at 2) carries over untouched. var = demand_mean*theta and CV = sqrt(theta/demand_mean), so theta is a DISPERSION axis: theta=1 reproduces Poisson's variance exactly (mean=var), which is why the gamma branch is the same demand with the lattice removed rather than a different problem. Poisson structurally cannot carry this axis -- its variance is locked to its mean -- so opening theta is a capability the continuous rendering buys. Not swept yet: EXPERIMENT DESIGN, a later choice.

constants.name: beta
constants.desc: the objective's discount factor -- the paper's alpha (costs n periods out discounted by alpha^n, p.1783). A DESIGN choice, not a model claim: the paper fixes the form and not the value, and mdp.model declares the quantity's domain as real in [0, 1]. Named rather than written into the objective so an instance can render this model at another discount (upstream #68, v0.9.29); a value with no name cannot be overridden by an instance. Confirmed 0.95 at the Phase-A sign-off (`human_confirmed`), the same provenance as demand_mean and p_short. SWEPT since F12: `n3_l2_p09_b1`, `g1_n3_l2_p09_b1` and `verify_tiny_b1` render the same model undiscounted. Each twin is its OWN FRAME -- a different objective is a different problem, so no score crosses between a cell and its twin.

constants.name: dp_slack
constants.desc: spec 9.9 implementation slack for the `dp` benchmark: the band max(tolerance, z*SE) inside which a feasible arm scoring better than the reference is reported rather than failed. Named because ONE entry serves two renderings whose numerical error differs in size and in kind (upstream #68). 0.001 is the POISSON value: the decomposition is exact on the lattice and its only numerical caveat is the pmf truncated at dropped mass < 1e-9 per period, ~1e-4 in metric units over the horizon. The gamma instances override it -- see their entry.

state_variables.name: period
state_variables.desc: current period t; horizon ends when period == T

state_variables.name: stock
state_variables.desc: stock[k] = physical on-hand inventory at installation k+1 (0-indexed: stock[0] is the retailer, which may go negative when demand is backlogged; upper installations are non-negative). Exactly n_echelons long -- the width NAMES the chain length, so an instance renders the levels it has and there is no inert padding. Echelon stock is the running sum with the in-flight terms offset one level (Assumption 3); see the objective's holding component.

narrowed.to: integer lattice, under the `poisson` selection ONLY -- the base type is real, which is what the model layer declares (demand: distribution on [0, inf), the paper's density phi(t))
narrowed.by: selection: demand = poisson (integer support) + design: integer shipment quantities (the gym's discrete action lattices). Under the `gamma` selection NEITHER holds and the state is real-valued. Stating the lattice as the state variable's TYPE was an over-commitment: it put a rendering choice in the model's shape, contradicting this very clause, which already named the selection as the cause. Found while adding the continuous branch.

state_variables.name: pipe

narrowed.to: integer lattice, under the `poisson` selection ONLY -- the base type is real, which is what the model layer declares (demand: distribution on [0, inf), the paper's density phi(t))
narrowed.by: selection: demand = poisson (integer support) + design: integer shipment quantities (the gym's discrete action lattices). Under the `gamma` selection NEITHER holds and the state is real-valued. Stating the lattice as the state variable's TYPE was an over-commitment: it put a rendering choice in the model's shape, contradicting this very clause, which already named the selection as the cause. Found while adding the continuous branch.

state_variables.desc: pipe[k][s] = units in flight into installation k+1, landing after s+1 more arrival events. BOTH axes name a scenario constant -- n_echelons links, each exactly leadtime slots -- so an instance renders precisely the shape it selects and there is no cap on either dimension. The A event shifts every link by slice-and-concat; a dispatch enters at the last slot. Quantified over k, not enumerated: the per-link rule is stated once.

info_fields.name: demand
info_fields.desc: realized retailer demand this period (D event)

placement.rationale: no later transition reads it; demand is i.i.d. across periods so it carries no predictive content, and neither observation mode exposes it

info_fields.name: arrived
info_fields.desc: arrived[k] = units that landed at installation k+1 this period

info_fields.name: shipped
info_fields.desc: shipped[k] = units actually moved into installation k+1 this period, after clipping to what the level above held

decisions.name: ship

type.rationale: a shipment quantity; continuous encoding with integer feasibility, so Poisson demand keeps every stock integral and the DP reference stays exact rather than gridded

bounds.rationale: ship_max = 200 = 20 x mean demand: an ACTION-SCALE cap, not a physical limit -- it only has to sit safely above any shipment a sensible policy would make (mean demand is 10). Carried as a bare constant so instances that move demand_mean resize it too (verify_tiny overrides to 40). Confirmed at the Phase-A sign-off.

narrowed.to: bounded [0, ship_max]; integer feasibility under the `poisson` selection ONLY
narrowed.by: implementation: ship_max action-scale cap + design: integer quantities so the DP reference is exact on the lattice rather than gridded. Under `gamma` the quantity is real and the DP reference is a GRID APPROXIMATION, so its benchmark role cannot be `exact` on that branch.

decisions.desc: ship[k] = quantity dispatched on link k this period, one per link, all links moving simultaneously. Width NAMES the chain length (dim: n_echelons), so the action is exactly as wide as the instance has links. Link k draws from installation k+2 and is clipped to what that installation holds; the TOP link (k = n_echelons-1) draws from the unlimited outside supplier and is capped only by ship_max.

uncertainty_slots.name: demand

poisson.desc: fixed-rate Poisson retailer demand, i.i.d. and stationary across periods. Both the family and the STATIONARITY are selections/design: the paper's section 2 poses a general density φ(t) and its parenthetical explicitly permits per-period distributions ('The demand distributions may actually differ from period to period') -- an earlier desc misquoted the paper as holding the distribution fixed. No draw spec: under THIS selection the slot carries no world latent.

gamma.desc: DEFAULT. Continuous retailer demand, i.i.d. and stationary across periods. This is the paper's OWN model: section 2 poses a general density phi(t), so the continuous rendering is the faithful one and the integer lattice is the narrowing (see `poisson`). Moment-matched to Poisson(demand_mean) at theta=1, so the two branches differ in lattice and in nothing else. Gamma rather than lognormal because it is closed under convolution at fixed scale: lead-time demand over L periods is exactly Gamma(L*demand_mean/theta, theta), which is the quantity the Clark-Scarf decomposition needs, so the demand side of the DP stays analytic and only the value function is gridded. Generator is `FamilyDemand`, the domain's family-driven zero-code path -- the differential adapter already routes any non-`poisson` candidate to it, so this branch needed no new generator class. That the extension point was there and worked is a fact about the original build, not a coincidence.

uncertainty_slots.desc: retailer demand, the only stochastic primitive in the model

updates: stock = [stock[k] + pipe[k][0] for k in range(n_echelons)]
shipped = [ship[k] if k == n_echelons - 1 else min(ship[k], stock[k + 1]) for k in range(n_echelons)]
stock = [stock[k] - (shipped[k - 1] if k >= 1 else 0) for k in range(n_echelons)]
pipe = [pipe[k][:leadtime - 1] + [pipe[k][leadtime - 1] + shipped[k]] for k in range(n_echelons)]

per_step_components.name: holding
per_step_components.expr: h_install[0] * max(0, stock[0]) + sum([h_install[k] * stock[k] for k in range(1, n_echelons)]) + sum([h_install[k + 1] * sum(pipe[k]) for k in range(n_echelons - 1)])
per_step_components.desc: echelon holding on end-of-period ECHELON STOCK, per Assumption 3: costs at a level are a function of the stock at that level plus all stock at a LOWER level or IN TRANSIT TO A LOWER level. So stock in transit TO installation k+1 belongs to echelon k+2, not k+1 -- it is charged the same rate as stock sitting at its source (h_install[k+1]), and only starts paying the destination's higher rate once it lands. Stock in transit to the TOP level is in no echelon's stock at all (it is on order, not yet in the system); h_install is 0 above the chain, which gives exactly that with no special case. Charging position k the cumulative rate H_k = sum of h_j for j >= k+1 is algebraically identical to charging each echelon its own h_k on echelon stock x_k. NB echelon STOCK (what holding is charged on) is not echelon POSITION (what f_n(u) optimizes over) -- the paper keeps in-transit w1 as its own coordinate, C_n(x1, w1, x2), precisely because of this.

per_step_components.name: shortage
per_step_components.desc: the paper's Eq. (1) shortage term, charged on end-of-period backlog at the retailer

per_step_components.name: shipping
per_step_components.expr: sum([c_ship[k] * shipped[k] for k in range(n_echelons)])
per_step_components.desc: linear shipping/ordering cost on executed shipments; identically 0 under every current scenario (c_ship = 0 by design) -- rendered so the model's c_k is expressible, per the model/design boundary (clark_scarf.model.json)

invariants.name: retailer_balance
invariants.desc: retailer stock changes only by what lands from above and what customers take

invariants.name: conservation
invariants.expr: close(sum(stock) + sum([sum(pipe[k]) for k in range(n_echelons)]), sum(prev.stock) + sum([sum(prev.pipe[k]) for k in range(n_echelons)]) + shipped[n_echelons - 1] - demand)
invariants.desc: nothing enters or leaves the system except what the top link brings in from the outside supplier and what demand takes out at the retailer. Stated over the whole state now that there is no padding to exclude.

invariants.name: upper_levels_non_negative
invariants.desc: only the retailer can go negative: no installation ever ships more than it holds

features.expr: [[pipe[k][s] for k in range(n_echelons)] for s in range(leadtime - 1)]
[sum([stock[j] for j in range(k + 1)]) + sum([sum(pipe[j]) for j in range(k)]) for k in range(n_echelons)]
[[sum([pipe[j][s] for j in range(k + 1)]) for k in range(n_echelons)] for s in range(leadtime - 1)]
[[pipe[k][s] for k in range(n_echelons)] for s in range(leadtime - 1)]
[sum([stock[j] for j in range(k + 1)]) + sum([sum(pipe[j]) for j in range(k)]) for k in range(n_echelons)]
[[sum([pipe[j][s] for j in range(k + 1)]) for k in range(n_echelons)] for s in range(leadtime - 1)]

action_modes.name: ship_discrete
action_modes.desc: DEFAULT. One categorical head per link (MultiDiscrete); the bin index IS the shipment quantity in whole units, 0 .. 4x mean demand. Discrete because the problem is: demand is Poisson and every stock is integral (the decisions are marked `integer`), so a fractional shipment would put non-integers into an integer state and cost the DP reference its exactness. A categorical head also carries no action-scale hazard -- it reweights rather than crawling a Gaussian mean, so every quantity is reachable from the first update.

action_modes.name: ship_fraction
action_modes.desc: The decision is a FRACTION of what the source can supply: the action IS the fraction: q = a * ship_capacity[k] with a in [0,1], no affine remap, so an action of 0.7 reads as '70% of what my source can supply' wherever it is printed -- which matters because this domain does policy readbacks (spec 14). ONE mode for both renderings. Rounding is keyed on the DEMAND DISTRIBUTION, not on the action mode: under a discrete selection the shipment is rounded half-up so stocks stay on the lattice and the DP reference keeps its exactness; under a continuous one nothing rounds and distinct actions give distinct quantities. That is `narrowed` on this decision implemented rather than encoded structurally -- it already reads 'integer feasibility under the `poisson` selection ONLY'. A separate discrete-fraction mode was built and then removed: a fraction is one decision, and giving it two action modes puts a rendering choice into the action space, the same category error `narrowed` exists to prevent. Half-UP and not numpy's rint (half-to-even), which against a state-varying cap hands even quantities three times the prior mass of odd ones -- a parity bias invisible in any aggregate score. A symmetric [-1,1] box was used first, reasoning that SB3's Gaussian starts at raw 0 so [0,1] would start by shipping nothing. That imported a caveat from `ship`, where raw 0 meant 'ship nothing' AND the useful range was ~1.5% of the box: the failure was the unreachability, not the zero, and here the box IS the useful range. What the two actually trade is the initial action distribution -- SB3 clips an unbounded Gaussian, so [0,1] puts ~50% of initial mass at 0 and [-1,1] ~16% -- and [-1,1] loses that trade under the ship_capacity cap, because it would centre the TOP link at half of ship_max, ten times mean demand, every episode at initialization. The fraction is of ship_capacity UNCLAMPED -- the IR's own per-link bound, nothing added and no constant invented. Below the top link that is the source's on-hand stock, so a=+1 is 'ship everything available' in every state (LV1: the useful extreme keeps a CONSTANT address); on the top link it is ship_max, the declared bound [0, ship_max]. Echelon-free (#E11/FM3): it reads ship_capacity, raw on-hand, never echelon_position. No mask applies or is needed -- the fraction is taken OF the cap, so `feasibility_strategy: clip` never fires (LV3). KNOWN CONSEQUENCE, carried deliberately: ship_max is 20x mean demand, so the top link's useful region occupies a narrow part of the action range and the encoding inherits `ship`'s action-scale hazard there -- left as a TRAINING question for an L0/L1 result rather than pre-engineered away. Two earlier bounds were withdrawn: a min(available, 4x mean) clamp, and a constant justified from the range of shipments the DP POLICY makes, which sets the action space from the reference solution (#E11/FM3 one layer down) and samples only states the DP visits, not the depleted ones an agent trains through.

action_modes.name: ship_absolute
action_modes.desc: NAIVE CONTROL. Identity on [0, ship_max] -- the paper-native encoding, and the measurement that motivates every other mode here. It carries the action-scale hazard by construction: SB3's Gaussian starts at raw 0 with std 1, so early actions cover ~[0,3] of a box 20x mean demand wide, and raw 0 means 'ship nothing' -- measured at 22560 against an optimum of 982. Renamed from `ship` so the contrast with `ship_fraction` is in the name: absolute quantity vs fraction of what the source can supply.

reward_modes.name: neg_cost
reward_modes.desc: negated per-step cost.total (sense=minimize, reward is maximized)

requires_memory.rationale: fully observed: demand is i.i.d. with a fixed known rate and there is no world latent, so the current stock vector is a sufficient statistic under either observation mode

obs_normalization.rationale: stock entries are stationary and of similar magnitude within a mode, but the echelon mode's running sums span a wider range than the raw mode's per-level stocks; spec 8.3 says normalize

eval_metrics.name: undiscounted_cost
eval_metrics.source: objective candidate, declined at Phase A: the undiscounted total was the alternative to beta = 0.95 and is kept as a report-only column
eval_metrics.desc: total cost with no discounting. Describes, never decides.

assumptions_log: Serial chain from Clark & Scarf (1960) sections 2-3: demand originates only at installation 1 (Assumption 1), shipping is linear with no setup cost (Assumption 2), one-period costs are functions of ECHELON stock rather than installation stock (Assumption 3), and every echelon backlogs excess demand (Assumption 4).

Chain length n_echelons is a swept axis over {2, 3, 4}. One period of transit per link, so a level adding no holding increment is exactly one period of pure delay: chain length subsumes the lead-time axis, and the paper's own two-echelon-with-two-period-lead example is a three-level chain with a free middle.

Action width is N, one shipment per link, as section 3 counts it ('two decisions are made' for two installations) and as Eq. (14) minimizes (over y and z). The 2N that appears in this paper is the (S_n, s_n) pair per echelon under a setup cost -- a description of the SOLUTION, not the width of the decision.

The state is carried in RAW installation coordinates and echelon stock is derived as a running sum. The two are related by an invertible linear map, so this is an implementation choice with no bearing on the model; raw was chosen because the availability constraint is then a per-component box (ship_k <= stock at the level above) rather than a coupled differencing condition.

Costs: purchase and shipping are FREE (c = c_ship = 0), isolating the holding-versus-shortage trade-off; linear purchase cost largely telescopes under backlogging, and inv_single sets c = 0.0 for the same reason. Echelon holding rates are h_retail = 1.0 at level 1 and h_echelon = 0.5 above; these enter as the cumulative per-installation rates h_install.
Objective discounts at beta = 0.95, the paper's alpha^n weighting (Phase A step 1, human_confirmed). Undiscounted total cost is retained as a report-only eval metric.

Demand is Poisson with a fixed rate of 10 -- chosen over 5 so integrality is fine-grained relative to the decision scale and does not contaminate the base-stock readback. No world latent: the paper holds the demand distribution fixed across the horizon.

Every episode starts with one period of cover at each installation (stock[k] = demand_mean), stated in raw coordinates; in echelon coordinates that reads x_k = k * demand_mean. This is not the optimum and hands the agent nothing -- it only starts the chain in flow, so the coordination problem is live from period 0 rather than after an N-period forced stockout.

The stock vector always carries n_levels_max = 4 slots; levels at index >= n_echelons are inert padding whose shipments are forced to 0 and whose stock is read by no cost or constraint. Padding exists only in the model file: both observation modes and the action mode are sliced to the live n_echelons, so no trained policy ever sees a dead input or emits a dead output.
Shipments are integer-valued: Poisson demand keeps every stock integral, and that is what keeps the DP reference exact rather than gridded.

Two observation modes, raw and echelon, are informationally identical (an invertible running sum). The campaign's headline question -- whether RL rediscovers the echelon structure -- is therefore a test of REPRESENTATION, not of information. An MLP can express a cumulative sum (a lower-triangular matrix of ones), so a raw-mode shortfall would be an optimization finding, not an impossibility.
Seed scheme v2 (spec 6.3): the single demand slot draws intrinsically at [period, 0, 1, episode_seed, seed_salt]. There are no world latents, so no meta-branch draws exist.

The exact DP reference is the Clark-Scarf decomposition itself, which section 3 states repeats at every echelon and which Theorems 1-2 prove optimal; it stays N one-dimensional problems rather than one N-dimensional problem. The verify_tiny instance is small enough to brute-force the full joint DP, so that optimality claim is CHECKED rather than assumed.

The DP truncates the Poisson pmf at a high quantile and renormalizes while the simulator does not, so the DP is optimal for a distribution differing from the simulated one by mass below 1e-9. Documented so the DP row is never read as unconditionally exact.

OBSERVATION MODES (gym layer, mutable): `raw` shows physical stock per installation plus in-flight stock; `echelon` shows the running sums applied COMPONENT-WISE -- cumsum(stock) and cumsum of EACH pipeline slot separately, never one sum over their total. A single running sum over the combined transit would be genuinely LOSSY at any leadtime >= 2 and would turn the headline experiment into a test of information rather than representation. Clark & Scarf's own state for that case, C_n(x1, w1, x2), likewise carries in-transit w1 separately from echelon stock. Both modes are sliced to the live n_echelons levels and prefixed by the normalized period (the horizon is finite, so the optimal critical numbers are time-varying). Guarded by clark_scarf_test.py::test_raw_and_echelon_are_a_pure_change_of_coordinates.

CORRECTION (post-freeze, re-signed): in-transit stock was initially charged the DESTINATION echelon's rate. Assumption 3 says a level's cost covers stock at that level plus stock at a lower level or in transit to a lower level -- so in transit TO level j is in echelon j+1, not echelon j, and is charged its SOURCE's rate until it lands. Stock in transit to the top level is in no echelon (on order, not yet in the system). The old form double-charged pipeline stock (2.0 vs 1.0 per period at n3_l2_p09) and, since the policy controls how much is in flight, biased the shipping incentive against moving stock downstream -- the exact trade-off the campaign measures. The `echelon` observation mode follows the same definition and keeps a separate cumulative in-transit block, so it stays an invertible re-coordinatization of `raw`.

ACTION ENCODING (gym layer, mutable): default is `ship_discrete`, a MultiDiscrete categorical head per link over whole-unit quantities 0..4x mean demand. Chosen because integrality is the problem's own (Poisson demand, integral stocks, decisions marked `integer`) and because a categorical head has no action-scale hazard. The continuous `ship` encoding was measured stuck near 'ship nothing' (~17-22k against an optimum of 982) after 300k steps; `ship_rel` (Gaussian recentred on mean demand) reached ~1082 at the same budget. inv_single reached the same conclusion for the same reason -- its default is `order_discrete`, citing its ESCALATION #E4.

ACTION ENCODING, final (gym layer): default is `target_discrete` -- the agent emits the echelon order-up-to level, not the shipment quantity. Chosen because in quantity coordinates the optimum is state-dependent while in target coordinates it is mid-horizon constant; measured as the largest single win of the campaign (ESCALATION #E9). `ship_discrete`, `ship_rel` and `ship` are retained as non-default modes and as evidence.

NOTATION (2026-08-17): schema/code names are the one canonical vocabulary. Paper correspondence is recorded, not adopted, in mdp.model.notation (verified against the in-repo reprint): pipe slots = the paper's w_j; leadtime = lambda (never L -- the paper's L(x) is the one-period cost); discount_factor = alpha; h_install/p_short/c_ship = h/p/c_1; our forward t = the paper's n periods-remaining via n = T - t.

benchmarks.name: dp
benchmarks.basis: the Clark & Scarf decomposition (Theorems 1-2): the chain solved as N one-dimensional problems, each with Theorem 2's induced penalty. EXACT as an algorithm; the one numerical caveat is that the Poisson pmf is truncated at a high quantile (dropped mass < 1e-9 per period) while the simulator's sampler is not, so the bar may be optimistic by at most ~1e-4 in metric units over the 50-period horizon (1e-9 x p_short x a generous demand ceiling x T). Optimality is not taken on the theorems' word: clark_scarf_dp_exactness.py brute-forces the full joint state on verify_tiny and the gap is 0.000000 (ESCALATION #E1, which is where a 30%-suboptimal first draft was caught). SCOPE, since v0.4 gained a second demand candidate: this role describes the `poisson` branch, where the lattice is the true state space and the decomposition is provably optimal on it. Under `gamma` the SAME solver is fed a binned density -- mean exact at every horizon, variance inflated by exactly 1/12 per aggregation (Sheppard's correction, the variance of a uniform over one lattice cell) -- so what it returns is a real, near-optimal policy rather than the optimum, which is role `feasible` by the taxonomy, not `exact`. A Benchmark entry carries ONE role and has no per-instance scoping, so this cannot be stated in the IR today: UPSTREAM PROPOSAL owed (a role that depends on which catalog candidate an instance selects). Until then, do NOT run the §9.9 ordering gate with --ir on a g*_ cell: it would read `exact` and call a legitimate win over a 1/12-inflated bar a defect. No gamma DP arm exists on any leaderboard yet, so the claim above is true of everything currently scored. TOLERANCE IS PER INSTANCE (upstream #68, v0.9.29): `dp_slack` is 0.001 on the poisson instances, where that caveat is the whole of it, and 2.0 on the gamma ones, where this same code feeds the lattice recursion a BINNED density. There the bar is a policy computed from a distribution the simulator does not draw from, so its critical numbers can sit a full lattice unit off the continuous optimum's; the worst single-unit target perturbation measured on g1_n3_l2_p09 costs 1.75 (0.176% of the bar), and 2.0 covers it. On the lattice no such term exists -- the targets are optimal there, not approximate.
benchmarks.source: spec §9.9 role; declared 2026-08-17 against upstream #23, filed from this campaign

benchmarks.name: echelon
benchmarks.basis: echelon base-stock WITHOUT the decomposition -- the echelon idea alone, targets fitted per level. Feasible by construction: it runs under the real information set.

benchmarks.name: local
benchmarks.basis: local (installation) base-stock: each level reorders to its own target, ignoring the level below. Pre-1960 practice, and the control the echelon idea is priced against.

benchmarks.name: random
benchmarks.basis: uniform random shipments within the action box -- the floor, present so the ladder has a bottom and a broken eval is visible.

tier2.structure: the echelon coordinate transform, on the continuous branch
tier2.claim: Same claim as the primary entry, asked where it can finally be asked cleanly. ESCALATION #E11 voided the discrete campaign's answer because `target_discrete`'s decode computed the echelon position from simulator state, so the transform was supplied through the ACTION interface whatever the observation was; that left only `ship_discrete`, which is echelon-free but spends ~half its categorical head on clipped-equivalent actions. A continuous fraction-of-capacity action is echelon-free AND well-conditioned -- it reads ship_capacity, raw on-hand at the source, never echelon_position -- so it is the first instrument that is neither disqualified nor handicapped.
